correctness.rationale: The local prime-power formulas give strict opposite inequalities for exponent one versus exponent at least two, leaving precisely p^2 q, p^3 q, and p q r^2 when Omega<=4. For the first two patterns, equality forces p-1|2 and yields only 20 and 45 after checking primality. For p<q both singleton primes and r squared, the equality forces r<p<q, q|r^2+1, p|q+1, and t(k+1)=r-1 with t=(r^2+1)/q and k=(q+1)/p>=2. Then t|gcd(r-1,r^2+1)|2; r=2 is impossible; for odd r, t=2 and r-3|12 force r=7 and q=25, contradiction. This covers all prime values without a size bound. Standard-library exact finite enumeration checks 737448 low-Omega integers through 10^6 and 2262 primes in the necessary-factor reduction.

value.rationale: This is a motivated natural complete classification by Omega, the total prime-factor count, for the published unitary–exponential divisor-sum equality problem. Omega=4 is the first complexity level admitting a nonsquarefree integer with three distinct prime supports; the fresh p q r^2 obstruction is structurally nontrivial and not a renamed two-prime corollary. It determines the complete equality set at that level, with a universal proof independent of numerical cutoffs. It does not claim to resolve the global infinitude question.
